name: Reserva
pairings: Roast meats, grilled lamb, duck à l'orange, pork, wild mushrooms, casseroles, Iberian ham, mature cheeses
notes: 100% Tempranillo, hand-harvested (Gimileo & Haro). 18 months in medium-toast American oak, bottled unfiltered. Deep ruby with tawny highlights; black fruit, liquorice, violet, vanilla, sweet spice, toasted bread. Drinking now; will evolve gracefully for 8–12 years.

name: Munfrina
pairings: Charcuterie, pasta with meat sauce, wood-fired pizza, roasted chicken, grilled pork chops
notes: 100% Dolcetto. A vibrant, fruit-forward red with bright acidity, dark cherry notes, and a classic bitter almond finish; typical drinking window used for young Dolcetto.

name: Shiraz
pairings: grilled steaks, barbecue ribs, burgers, pepperoni pizza, mature cheddar
notes: 100% Shiraz. A medium-bodied, approachable wine with ripe plum, blackberry, and subtle spice notes. The drinking window is based on typical ranges for entry-level commercial Australian Shiraz, which is designed for early consumption.

name: Bourgogne Passetoutgrains
pairings: Charcuterie, cold cuts, roasted poultry, simple pork dishes
notes: A traditional blend of Pinot Noir and Gamay. As a light Bourgogne Passetoutgrains intended for youthful consumption, this 1983 vintage is now well past its prime drinking window.

name: L'Amour Toujours
pairings: Grilled steak, roast lamb, aged cheddar, venison, hearty stews
notes: Bordeaux-style red blend from the Allée Bleue estate (founded 1690), Stellenbosch. Award-winning bottling (Double Platinum, National Wine Challenge Champion, Top 100 SA Wines). Drink window is an estimate for a premium Cape Bordeaux blend of this vintage, not a producer-published figure.

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
pairings: Grilled beef, lamb chops, hearty stews, aged cheeses
notes: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon. Produced by Viña Caliterra Ltda., Santiago. Well past typical drinking window for this tier of Chilean Cab.

name: Carte d'Or Muscadet Sèvre et Maine Sur Lie
region: Muscadet Sèvre et Maine AOC, Loire, France
pairings: Oysters, mussels, grilled fish, shrimp, goat cheese
notes: 100% Melon de Bourgogne. Sur lie ageing adds richness. Le Cleray, 12% alc. Past typical window but top Muscadet can surprise with age.

name: Don Melchor Private Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon
pairings: Prime rib, roast lamb, venison, truffled dishes, aged Gruyère
notes: Flagship icon Cabernet Sauvignon from Concha y Toro. One of Chile's most celebrated wines. Well-cellared bottles may still drink, though past optimal window.

name: Pomerol
pairings: Roast duck, filet mignon, truffled risotto, soft-ripened cheeses
notes: Merlot-dominant Pomerol. JP Moueix. 1989 is a legendary Bordeaux vintage. At or past peak but could still offer pleasure if well stored.

name: St-Émilion Grand Cru
pairings: Roast lamb, braised beef, duck confit, mature Comté
notes: Moueix proprietor. Merlot/Cabernet Franc blend. Past peak drinking window.

name: St-Émilion Grand Cru
region: St-Émilion Grand Cru Classé, Bordeaux, France
pairings: Roast beef, lamb, game birds, aged hard cheeses
notes: Vicomte P. de Lesquen, proprietor. St-Émilion Grand Cru Classé. Past typical drinking window.

name: No. 99 Baco Noir
pairings: BBQ ribs, burgers, pulled pork, pizza, cheddar
notes: 100% Baco Noir. 12.5% alc. A fruity, medium-bodied Canadian red best enjoyed young.

name: No. 99 Chardonnay
pairings: Grilled chicken, creamy pasta, lobster, brie
notes: 100% Chardonnay. 13.0% alc. Best enjoyed young.

name: NeroMàccarj
pairings: Grilled sausages, pasta alla Norma, braised lamb, pecorino
notes: 100% Nero d'Avola. Premium single-vineyard Sicilian red from a top producer. Past peak but could still surprise.

name: Cyane
pairings: Seafood, grilled fish, light salads, fresh mozzarella
notes: Siracusa DOC Bianco. Named after the nymph Cyane. From Pupillo estate in Syracuse, Sicily.

name: Cuvée Prestige Cabernet Sauvignon
pairings: Grilled steak, roast beef, lamb chops, semi-hard cheeses
notes: Grand Vin de Bordeaux. Véronique Barthe, vigneronne. Mis en bouteille au château. HVE certified.

name: Gewurztraminer Réserve
pairings: Foie gras, Munster cheese, spicy Asian cuisine, fruit tarts
notes: 100% Gewurztraminer. Réserve. Scherwiller. Aromatic Alsatian white with lychee, rose petal, and spice notes.

name: Re Federico
pairings: Grilled meats, pasta with ragù, aubergine parmigiana, aged pecorino
notes: Siracusa DOC Rosso. Likely Nero d'Avola-based. From Pupillo estate in Syracuse, Sicily.

name: Bordeaux
pairings: Grilled meats, roast chicken, charcuterie, mild cheeses
notes: Appellation Bordeaux Contrôlée. Caves de Rauzan. Bouteille à la Propriété.

name: Sancerre Les Baronnes
pairings: Goat cheese (Crottin de Chavignol), oysters, grilled white fish, asparagus
notes: 100% Sauvignon Blanc. Chavignol. Mis en bouteille au Domaine. Well past typical window.

name: Grange Bin 95
pairings: Prime rib, slow-braised short ribs, venison, aged cheddar, dark chocolate
notes: Australia's most iconic wine. Predominantly Shiraz. Dedicated to Max Schubert (1915–1994). Bottle No. AV762. Developed from observations of Bordeaux first-growth techniques, matured in new American oak hogsheads. Will age for decades.

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
pairings: Grilled ribeye, braised short ribs, roast lamb, aged Gouda
notes: Premium Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon. 14.4% alc. Should still be drinking well if properly cellared.

name: St-Émilion Grand Cru
pairings: Roast duck, filet mignon, lamb, truffled dishes, Époisses
notes: Vauthier, viticulteur à St-Émilion. 1989 is a legendary Bordeaux vintage. At or past peak.

name: Meursault
pairings: Lobster thermidor, roast chicken with cream sauce, Comté, scallops
notes: 100% Chardonnay. Domaine Faiveley, Nuits-Saint-Georges. Négociant-éleveur. Well past typical window but great Meursault can age.

name: Barolo
pairings: Braised beef, risotto with truffles, game, aged Parmigiano-Reggiano
notes: 100% Nebbiolo. La Morra. 13.5% alc. Estate bottled. Past peak but Barolo can surprise with long life.

name: Terrunyo Carmenere Block 27
region: DO Peumo, Valle del Cachapoal, Chile
pairings: Grilled lamb, beef empanadas, slow-cooked stews, smoked Gouda
notes: Entre Cordilleras, Peumo Vineyard. Premium single-vineyard Carmenere. Block 27 designates specific terroir within the estate.

name: St-Émilion Grand Cru
pairings: Roast lamb, duck confit, beef bourguignon, mature cheeses
notes: Grand Vin de Bordeaux. Mestreguilhem proprietaire, St Laurent des Combes. Mis en bouteille au château. 2016 is an excellent Bordeaux vintage.

name: Old Vine Pinotage
pairings: Braai (SA barbecue), bobotie, grilled sausages, smoked meats
notes: Old vine Pinotage from Piekenierskloof. Allée Bleue estate founded 1690. Eike Daasen.

name: Sassicaia
pairings: Bistecca alla fiorentina, roast lamb, wild boar ragù, aged Pecorino Toscano
notes: Marchesi Incisa della Rocchetta. Cabernet Sauvignon/Cabernet Franc blend. Italy's original Super Tuscan, Bolgheri's most iconic wine.

name: Barolo
pairings: Braised beef, truffle risotto, osso buco, aged Parmigiano-Reggiano
notes: 100% Nebbiolo. La Morra. Estate bottled. Should still be in a fine drinking window.

name: Sassicaia
pairings: Bistecca alla fiorentina, roast lamb, wild boar ragù, aged Pecorino Toscano
notes: Marchesi Incisa della Rocchetta. Cabernet Sauvignon/Cabernet Franc blend. Tenuta San Guido, Bolgheri. Should still be drinking beautifully.

name: St-Émilion 1er Grand Cru Classé A
pairings: Roast lamb, filet mignon, truffle dishes, foie gras, aged Comté
notes: 1er Grand Cru Classé A. Héritiers Fourcaud-Laussac. One of Bordeaux's most legendary estates. Predominantly Cabernet Franc and Merlot. At or past peak but iconic bottles can endure.

name: L'Authentique
pairings: Grilled meats, duck, cassoulet, semi-hard cheeses
notes: Francs Côtes de Bordeaux. Charming label featuring a stag in a beret and marinière. Right Bank Bordeaux blend.

name: Nubiola Barbaresco
pairings: Braised beef, risotto with porcini, roast veal, tajarin pasta, aged cheeses
notes: 100% Nebbiolo. Pelissero Giorgio, Treiso. Single-vineyard Barbaresco. Young — will benefit from cellaring.

name: Valpolicella Classico Superiore
region: Valpolicella Classico Superiore DOC, Veneto, Italy
pairings: Pizza, pasta with tomato sauce, grilled vegetables, light meats
notes: Corvina, Rondinella, Molinara blend. Historic label edition. Drink young.

name: Valpolicella Ripasso Classico Superiore
region: Valpolicella Ripasso Classico Superiore DOC, Veneto, Italy
pairings: Grilled red meats, pasta with meat ragù, hard cheeses, risotto
notes: Azienda Agricola. Ripasso method — re-fermented on Amarone grape skins for added body and complexity.

name: Sforzato dell'Orco
region: Sforzato di Valtellina DOCG, Lombardy, Italy
pairings: Braised meats, game, polenta taragna, bresaola, aged Bitto cheese
notes: 100% Nebbiolo (locally called Chiavennasca). Appassimento method — grapes partially dried before pressing. Rich, complex alpine Nebbiolo.

name: Tradizione del Nonno Riserva
region: Primitivo di Manduria DOP, Puglia, Italy
pairings: Grilled lamb, orecchiette with sausage, eggplant parmigiana, aged provolone
notes: 100% Primitivo. Riserva. Sava, Italy. Full-bodied, rich southern Italian red.

name: Patina Cabernet Franc Reserve
pairings: Roast pork, goulash, grilled meats, paprika dishes, aged cheeses
notes: 100% Cabernet Franc Reserve. Hungarian producer. Label text in Hungarian describes the wine's character.

name: Guado al Tasso
pairings: Bistecca alla fiorentina, roast lamb, wild boar, aged Pecorino, truffled dishes
notes: Tenuta Guado al Tasso. Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot blend. Antinori's flagship Bolgheri Super Tuscan.
